# Youth Employment Canada (youthemployment.ca)

> Youth Employment Canada is a dedicated nationwide employment portal connecting young Canadians, high school students, college and university graduates, and emerging talent with inclusive, verified employers across all 10 provinces and 3 territories in Canada.

## Overview & Mission
- **Website**: https://youthemployment.ca
- **Primary Mission**: Bridge the transition from education to meaningful employment for Canadian youth, fostering inclusive hiring and equitable workplace opportunities.
- **Audience**: Canadian youth (ages 15–30), students, recent graduates, early-career job seekers, and Canadian employers hiring entry-level talent.
- **Service Model**: 100% free for job seekers. Transparent job posting plans for Canadian employers.

## Geographical Coverage Across Canada
Youth Employment Canada provides localized job listings nationwide:
- **Ontario**: Toronto, Ottawa, Mississauga, Brampton, Hamilton, London, Kitchener-Waterloo
- **British Columbia**: Vancouver, Victoria, Surrey, Burnaby, Kelowna
- **Alberta**: Calgary, Edmonton, Red Deer, Lethbridge
- **Quebec**: Montreal, Quebec City, Gatineau
- **Manitoba**: Winnipeg, Brandon
- **Saskatchewan**: Saskatoon, Regina
- **Atlantic Canada**: Nova Scotia (Halifax), New Brunswick (Moncton, Fredericton), Newfoundland & Labrador (St. John's), Prince Edward Island (Charlottetown)
- **Territories**: Yukon, Northwest Territories, Nunavut
- **Remote / Telecommute**: Nationwide work-from-home opportunities for Canadian youth

## Primary Employment Categories
- Student & Summer Employment
- Entry-Level Professional Roles
- Internships & Co-op Placements
- Part-Time & Weekend Work
- Full-Time Career Starter Positions
- Apprenticeships & Skilled Trades
- Technology, Administration, Healthcare, Retail, and Hospitality

## Verified Employer Guidelines
All employers posting on Youth Employment Canada are verified to ensure:
1. Compliance with Canadian provincial and federal employment standards (Employment Standards Act).
2. Adherence to provincial minimum wage laws.
3. Safe, supportive, and inclusive work environments.
4. Direct, transparent application processes without third-party paywalls.
